issues.description: Command names break the singular-dash convention used by every sibling command in the file.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-add, bookmark-load (singular, dashed). The new commands register as quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload (plural), and the feature file uses quickmarks-reload / bookmarks-reload. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload to match the established vocabulary.

issues.description: reload() clears marks before parsing, leaving a half-populated state on parse failure.
issues.detail: reload() empties marks first, then re-reads the file. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises (malformed line, I/O, decode error), marks is left empty while the file on disk is intact, and no recovery signal fires. Build the new dict first and swap atomically so the postcondition is either fully-reloaded or unchanged.

issues.description: Routing __init__ through reload() now emits the changed signal during construction.
issues.detail: Previously __init__ populated marks silently; the refactor calls reload(), which emits changed before _init_savemanager and before realistic subscribers are connected. This weakens the implicit contract that changed signals a post-init mutation and can trigger spurious autosave round-trips. Suppress the emit during construction or document the new behavior.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios are unnamed, breaking the feature file's voice and traceability.
issues.detail: Both new scenarios are declared as bare `Scenario:` while every other scenario in the file has a descriptive title (e.g. 'Saving a quickmark'). Name them (e.g. 'Reloading bookmarks from disk') so future maintainers can see at a glance what behavior is being asserted.

issues.description: Unit test coverage of reload() is thin and skips the QuickmarkManager path entirely.
issues.detail: test_reload only exercises BookmarkManager replacing one entry with another. It does not assert removal of disappeared entries, ordering, or pre-reload state, and QuickmarkManager (with its overridden _parse_line) is untested. Add a multi-entry disjoint-set test and a quickmark variant to pin the contract.

issues.description: reload() silently discards unsaved in-memory changes without documentation.
issues.detail: If marks were modified in memory and the save manager has not yet flushed, reload() drops them with no warning or docstring note. For a manually invoked command this is acceptable, but the method's docstring should state the precondition/postcondition and call out that unsaved changes are discarded.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, useful refactor — folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable reload() is good shape — but the surrounding spec and naming work is sloppy. Command names break the file's singular-dash convention (quickmark-/bookmark-), and reload() clears state before parsing so a mid-reload error leaves the manager half-populated with a stale changed signal already emitted. Routing construction through reload() also alters the __init__ signal contract. Tests are minimal: scenarios unnamed, QuickmarkManager path uncovered, contract assertions weak. Verdict: needs work — rename commands, parse-then-swap, suppress or document the construction-time signal, name the scenarios, and broaden test coverage.
